US commerce secretary faces sack as questions emerge over senior Trump officials’ knowledge of alleged Chinese spy’s ties to Jensen Huang
The US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, is facing growing pressure over his apparent lack of action over the Nvidia spying scandal as other Trump administration officials publicly raise questions over his decisions.
Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, blamed Lutnick’s commerce department for the fact the US had not imposed export restrictions on certain Nvidia chips to China.
Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday, and was replaced on an interim basis by the company’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress , after reports emerged of his multiple affairs, most importantly with Alice Huang (no relation), who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.
White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be fired, the Associated Press reported, after it emerged that a US intelligence report about Huang’s relationship with the alleged spy was circulated among senior figures in the Trump administration .
Lutnick is now scheduled to testify before Congress next month, just days after the ousted Nvidia chief answers lawmakers’ questions on Capitol Hill.
Lutnick is also facing criticism for a delay by the commerce department in adding Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is associated with Alice Huang and has bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips in recent years, to Washington’s blacklist of companies that the US considers a risk to national security despite reported concerns within the administration.
Bessent has “for months” been in favor of putting Megaspeed on the blacklist – but Lutnick’s commerce department “has the pen”, Bessent told CNBC. “You will have to ask them about their internal process,” he added in an interview with the network on Friday.
John Curtis, a Utah Republican senator, said that Lutnick’s reported delay on export controls regarding Megaspeed “raises the question of whether the commerce department is acting in the best interests of the American people”.
The Republican senator John Cornyn told the Financial Times that there needed to be “a thorough investigation and accountability for the outrageous circumvention of national security export controls”, adding: “Heads should roll.”
The Senate Democratic leader, Chuck Schumer, said Jensen Huang and Nvidia must answer as to whether US security had been jeopardised, adding that the Trump administration also must account for what it did once it learned about his reported relationship with Alice Huang.
“Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the banking committee to address their questions,” Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News.
Trump’s close ties with Jensen Huang have also come under renewed scrutiny as a timeline of the saga started to emerge . The president called him two days before he stepped down and urged him to fight for his job, the New York Times has reported .
On Thursday, Schumer questioned what Trump knew when he personally invited Jensen Huang aboard Air Force One on a state visit to Beijing earlier this year, adding: “Americans deserve to know that those at the highest levels of power are putting America first, not their bottom line or their personal friendships.”
The House Democratic leader, Hakeem Jeffries, said he had demanded a classified briefing for all members of Congress about Nvidia.
Republican Tim Scott, the Senate banking committee chair, said he had sent letters asking Lutnick and Jensen Huang to appear before him, citing “recent reports [that] raise serious ‌concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology”.
The statement from Nvidia’s board of directors confirming Huang’s departure did not mention the spying scandal and personal-conduct revelations, instead paying tribute to his “profound” contributions to the company he cofounded.
Huang is reported to have had relationships with Alice Huang as well as an Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, according to the New York Times, and another, unnamed employee, according to Reuters.
The House foreign affairs chair, Brian Mast, a Republican, said on Thursday that congressional staff had spoken to Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for Huang’s testimony.
The House speaker, Mike Johnson, said on Thursday there was now growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China .
Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company important to the US race against ​China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to ‌limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does ‌not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.
“The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here,” Johnson told reporters ‌at the US Capitol, adding that he favoured limiting China’s access to the advanced technology. “I think there’s a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take.“
Chinese AI companies are now trying to secure Nvidia chip capacity outside China, amid growing concern that the gap in US export controls may now be closed after the scandal, people familiar with the matter told Reuters .
Beijing has also stepped up efforts to develop domestic alternatives, including through Huawei, although analysts say Chinese chips remain less efficient for training advanced AI models.
Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four bills on chip exports, according to statements issued since Monday.
On Chinese social media, many expressed surprise at what they see as Huang’s swift resignation, and mourned the sudden end of an era that lasted for more than three decades.
News of his resignation attracted more than 400m posts overnight on the Chinese microblogging platform Weibo.
Huang had enjoyed rock-star status in China, where his visits drew crowds seeking selfies and autographs and his casual outings became social-media sensations. During a January 2026 visit, opportunistic sellers advertised photographs with him for 25,000 yuan ($3,700), while a Beijing restaurant launched a special menu costing more than 400 yuan after he ate there.

How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet.
Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions.
Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy.
Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but it is not on a list of firms US companies are prevented from working with.
Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.
Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said some parts of the administration wanted more controls on trade with Megaspeed
Bessent said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China.
"President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.
Last year, the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of Nvidia's advanced AI chips into China, according to the New York Times. Megaspeed has been contacted for comment.
There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but separate reporting in the Financial Times said the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included.
"The story has been thus far of Jensen Huang's personal foibles," he told CNBC's Squawk Box programme , external .
"The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?
"It's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that."
Bessent's pointed comments are a rare instance of internal debate within the Trump administration spilling out into the public view, although tensions have reportedly simmered between Bessent and Lutnick in the past.
In 2024, the two reportedly jostled for the role of treasury secretary ahead of Trump's return to the White House, and last year the pair butted heads over the administration's tariff policy, accoprding to US media.

How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions
Huang has been summoned to testify before the Senate Banking Committee about his alleged affair with the former Megaspeed executive, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.
The commerce secretary has also been summoned to appear before the committee in December.
"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," committee chairman, Republican Senator Tim Scott posted on X.
Democrats on key congressional committees have asked the Commerce Department and Lutnick to keep all records relating to decisions to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced AI chips to Chinese companies, including all their communications with or about Nvidia and Jensen Huang.
Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E Neal and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden are starting investigations into the way Nvidia was allowed to sell these chips.
According to Neal and Wyden, Nvidia's advanced H200 chips could be sold to Chinese firms if they were first imported from their manufacturing facility in Taiwan into America for inspection.
A 25% tariff - a levy that is paid to the federal government - was imposed on those chips, under a section of the Trade Act that Neal and Wyden say is meant to allow the US president to take action against imports that risk national security.
"Trump's use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining US national security and putting Americans at risk," they said.

No passengers or crew were killed or critically hurt after a tanker collided with a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River, officials say
In what the city’s mayor declared a “miracle on the Mississippi”, all passengers were accounted for – with none killed or critically hurt – after a tanker collided with a river cruise ship docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon.
Thirty-two people were taken to local hospitals after the Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck American Cruise Lines’s American Heritage at about 12.30pm – but none of their injuries were considered critical, New Orleans’s mayor, Helena Moreno, said at a news conference.
Zero passengers or crew members were unaccounted for, Moreno said. She attributed that fact to a hectic but effective multi-agency rescue effort after the American Heritage was struck and a number of people ended up in the river, whose waters are cold and its currents are infamously perilous.
That “truly is a miracle on the Mississippi,” Moreno said near the scene of the crash, as a group of fellow officials around her applauded.
The American Heritage had about 129 passengers – in addition to crew members – onboard when it was hit, Port of New Orleans press secretary Kimberly Curth said in a statement.
About two hours before that, the American Heritage had docked at the port to begin passenger disembarkation, Curth said.
Officials did not immediately provide details about what caused the crash. Moreno said investigators would explore whether there was some loss of steering on the Atlantic Asphalt before it struck the American Heritage, as an emergency response source had said earlier – but that had not been immediately confirmed.
The website marinetraffic.com showed the Atlantic Asphalt’s path was seemingly uneventful as it went around the challenging Mississippi River bend near New Orleans’ Algiers Point neighborhood. It had just made it past the Crescent City Connection bridge linking New Orleans’ central business district and the community’s Algiers section when it began heading generally to its starboard – or right – side.
Video provided to Guardian reporting partner WWL Louisiana showed the Atlantic Asphalt then T-boned the side of the American Heritage. The cruise ship eventually slowly rolled on to its side where it was struck, according to the video, which the CBS affiliate obtained from Barry Kern, proprietor of Mardi Gras World, a tourist attraction near the scene of the crash.
One witness, Jamie Holford, told local NBC News affiliate WDSU that it took 15 minutes “from impact to where it rolled over”.
Maritime law expert Martin J Davies of New Orleans’ Tulane University told local Fox affiliate WVUE that the Atlantic Asphalt was fortunate to have not hit the Crescent City Connection, which could have endangered motorists on the bridge which is estimated to carry about 160,000 cars daily.
“This is obviously a really bad incident,” Davies said. “But it could also have struck the bridge, which it didn’t.”
A video from WDSU showed crew members of a tugboat working to pull people in lifejackets or holding on to flotation rings out of the river. An emergency response that drew in firefighters, US Coast Guard helicopter and boat crews, as well as port and city police – among others – also helped pull out people who ended up in the water in plain view of cameras and eyewitnesses.
One image on social media showed people climbing on the side of the cruise boat – specifically, on stateroom balconies – after it was struck, with chairs and tables strewn about after it evidently took on water.
An employee at the Ernest N Morial Convention Center next to the scene of Friday’s crash said she realized something was awry when she could see from her vantage point that the tip of the American Heritage was tilted. She then grasped the nature of situation when she heard desperate shrieks.
“People were screaming for help,” said the employee, who asked to not be named. She recalled how she and colleagues assembled wheelchairs, water and other items in case survivors would soon need them.
The American Heritage’s passengers were brought inside the New Orleans port’s administration building, next to the convention center.
At the news conference where officials then confirmed there were no casualties, Louisiana governor Jeff Landry echoed Moreno in invoking the term “miracle”, especially “when you think about the population that was on that cruise ship – and the ability for us to get them off and out of the water”.
“The Mississippi River is not some quiet pond,” Landry said. “There were challenges out there.”
With everyone accounted for, New Orleans’s US Coast Guard commander, Melanie Burnham, said the focus would shift to re-opening the river to traffic. It had been closed from mile markers 93 to 96 to facilitate rescue efforts.
US House majority leader Steve Scalise, a suburban New Orleans Republican, said on Friday that the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) would investigate the crash.
A statement from American Cruise Lines on Friday said “guests and crew were evacuated” from the American Heritage but did not elaborate. “We are deeply concerned for everyone involved,” the cruise operator’s statement added.
The American Heritage , a 300ft paddle-wheel ship, was built in 2015 and previously sailed as the Queen of the Mississippi. It has more than 80 staterooms and operates cruises on the Mississippi River, including ones which depart from New Orleans.
The Atlantic Asphalt is a oil tanker built in 2017 measuring approximately 160 meters in length and has a deadweight of 17,764 metric tons. It flies the flag of the Marshall Islands and is owned and commercially operated by Nave Shipping SA, a company registered in Liberia. Its maintenance, technical and safety operations are overseen by Singapore-based Thome Ship Management, according to online records.
The vessel, which had a next recorded destination for Singapore, does not appear on the international sanctions lists checked by maritime tracking services, including Magic Port .
However, it was previously fined C$7,800 by Canadian authorities for a violation of the Canada Shipping Act and related vessel pollution regulations.
The penalty, recorded on 11 August 2020, stemmed from an officer failing to properly carry out their duties while supervising a transfer operation aboard the oil tanker, according to the Canadian government.
To many in New Orleans, the crash involving the Atlantic Asphalt called to mind an episode nearby – nearly 30 years earlier – when a cargo ship struck a wharf adjacent to the city’s Riverwalk shopping center and Hilton Riverside hotel.
No deaths resulted from that case, which occurred on 14 December 1996 after the Liberian-registered Bright Field lost propulsion power, an NTSB report later said . But there were more than 60 injuries reported, including four which were considered serious.

The crash took place on a highway bordering Kaziranga National Park in the Golaghat district of Assam
At least 24 people have died and 11 others injured after a bus collided with a truck in Assam, north-east India.
The accident happened near Kaziranga National Park, a Unesco World Heritage site, and the injured have been admitted to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.
Several of the deceased are college students, according to Assam's rural development minister Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.
Bora added that witnesses reported one of the vehicles may have been speeding when the crash took place, but "the exact reason will be known after [an investigation]".
Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma wrote in a post on X that "the scale of this loss has shaken all of us".
He adds: "Our foremost priority now is to make sure the injured receive the best possible medical care without delay."
Family members of one of the victims pictured at the accident site
The bus was carrying passengers from Bokakhat and was headed towards Nagaon.
Bokakhat is best known as the gateway to Kaziranga National Park, famous for its one-horned rhinoceroses.
Nagaon is an important agricultural and commercial centre in central Assam, about 120km (74.5 miles) west of Bokakhat by road.
Lurinjyoti Gogoi, chief of a regional opposition party, said road safety has long been a major concern in the state.
Road accidents are responsible for thousands of deaths in India every year.
In 2023, 172,000 people lost their lives on Indian roads, or 474 a day – roughly one every three minutes.
Experts say the crisis is rooted not just in infrastructure but in human behaviour, enforcement gaps and systemic neglect.

At least 24 people have been ⁠⁠killed and 11 others injured, after a container truck collided with a bus in ⁠⁠India’s northeastern state of Assam, police said.
The crash happened on Friday on a highway in Golaghat district, near Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its one-horned rhinos, about 225km (140 miles) east of the state capital, Dispur.

Officials have not said if anyone was hurt after American Heritage was partially submerged with 129 passengers on board.
Dozens of passengers have been taken to hospital after a tanker struck a river cruise boat carrying 129 passengers in New Orleans, partially submerging the vessel, according to authorities.
The Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the American Heritage paddleboat on the Mississippi River on Friday at about 12:30pm local time (18:30 GMT), the Port of New Orleans said.
The cruise boat had docked about two hours earlier to begin letting passengers off.
New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday evening that all passengers on board the American Heritage were accounted for and that 32 were in local hospitals, none with critical injuries.
The Atlantic Asphalt tanker “lost control and collided into the cruise ship”, she said.
Passengers were disembarking when the boat “began to sink, and then eventually toppled over and flipped”, sending people into the water, she said.
Video from the scene showed the much larger tanker hitting the paddlewheel cruise boat as metal and glass crashed and crunched, according to The Associated Press news agency.
More than a dozen people in life jackets were dragged from the river, where the water temperature was 19 degrees Celsius (66 degrees Fahrenheit), onto nearby ships, while others stood near the railing as the boat listed further into the water.
“Surreal, that’s what that was,” one witness, Jamie Holford, told local television. “Fifteen minutes from impact to where it rolled over.”
Port police, the fire department, the coastguard and emergency medical staff are on the scene, and a triage area was set up inside the port’s administration building. The river was closed to vessel traffic.
American Cruise Lines, which operates the boat, said guests and crew had been evacuated and that it was “deeply concerned for everyone involved”.
The five-deck American Heritage, built in 2015, holds up to 150 passengers and was finishing an eight-day cruise to destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.
The 160-metre (520-foot) tanker was flying the flag of the Marshall Islands and was bound for New Orleans, according to the MarineTraffic tracker. It specialises in carrying asphalt and bitumen, according to the maritime periodical Marine Insights.
The cause of the collision, as well as whether the ship was carrying cargo, remains unknown.

Prime ministerial hopeful calls attempts to marginalise and smear Palestinian citizens of Israel ‘an anti-state act’.
Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot has accused caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fuelling a “racist and violent” campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel during the elections.
Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming Israel’s new government , posted a lengthy social media update on recent developments in Israel on Friday.
“Arab citizens of Israel make up 21 percent of the total population. Since the start of the election campaign, they have faced a racist and violent campaign of delegitimisation fuelled by the outgoing prime minister and his circle for political reasons,” Eisenkot wrote on X.
“The prime minister of Israel is the prime minister of all citizens, including those who did not vote for him,” he said. “Arab citizens of Israel are part of the Israeli story. The attempt to marginalise them and smear them as a group is an anti-state act.”
In Israel’s October 27 elections , Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.
Netanyahu repeatedly made unproven allegations of electoral fraud by Arab-majority parties – claims Israel’s own electoral authorities have rejected.
The caretaker leader has also repeatedly criticised Arab-led parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a “terror group” following the attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, despite all of the parties’ leaders condemning the Hamas-led assault.
“One can disagree with the representatives of the Arab parties, and one can even feel deep revulsion toward some of them, but one cannot, should not, and I will not allow an entire sector to be slandered,” Eisenkot said.
Arab-led parties have endorsed Eisenkot to replace Netanyahu. However, Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with those parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning the backing of the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.
On efforts to form an emergency government, Eisenkot reiterated that he wants to fulfil the mandate as soon as possible, adding “it would be a grave mistake not to do so”.
Eisenkot, who ran as Netanyahu’s main rival, has six weeks to form a new government.
While Netanyahu may be politically weakened, the prime minister is reported to be weighing military action against Iran , despite a lack of enthusiasm from the United States, his own military establishment, and Eisenkot, who has demanded that Netanyahu avoid any new escalation unless it is critical.
In Friday’s update, Eisenkot said he had met with Netanyahu and his military secretary on Thursday to discuss the security situation but provided no details.
Earlier in the week, Eisenkot said that he was open to including Netanyahu in his coalition. Eisenkot suggested Netanyahu’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was also welcome to join.
Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

The pact was signed after ​the President met Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim ‌bin Hamad ​Al Thani in Istanbul on ⁠Friday.
Turkiye and ⁠⁠Qatar have signed a mutual defence agreement after a meeting between Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim ‌‌bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul on Friday.
“President Erdogan stated that we would continue working together to prevent ⁠⁠the resurgence of ⁠⁠war in the Gulf region and establish a basis ⁠⁠for dialogue and ⁠⁠achieve peace,” ⁠⁠the Turkish presidency said in a statement on X.
Erdogan’s office said the agreement would “add a new dimension to relations between Turkiye and Qatar”, while the Qatari Emir praised the deal as a “strategic partnership”.
In a post on X, Sheikh Tamim wrote that he “discussed ways to build on what has been achieved and identify priorities for joint action in the coming period” during talks with President Erdogan.
A statement by the Amiri Diwan said multiple agreements were signed by the two governments, including a memorandum of understanding “on cooperation in the field of peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution”.
Speaking to Al Jazeera, security analyst Yusuf Alabarda said that since the start of the Iran war, countries in the region “are feeling the effects of the war and no one is feeling secure”.
“All the Gulf countries, but especially Qatar, understood that their security guarantees from the United States are not working properly. The Turkish troops in Qatar are very important but I can say that in the near term Turkish weapons and air defences might be deployed to Qatar to guarantee its safety, which is very important to Turkiye, so this agreement will help move forward these military deals,” Alabarda said.
In August, Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a regional defence pact under which the three countries would come to each other’s aid if one of them was attacked.
Ratified by the Turkish parliament last week, the pact links NATO member Turkiye, which has the alliance’s second-largest military, with Pakistan, the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state.
Turkiye has said the agreement is not aimed at any other country and remains open to other states, including Egypt.
In October, Qatar, Indonesia, Pakistan and Turkiye signed a multilateral memorandum of understanding on defence cooperation in Doha.
The agreement, known as “Badr”, aims to bolster cooperation between the participating countries.

The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into David Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences".
It comes after ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.
The Met said that the allegations being investigated are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian, but as "part of their investigation, detectives are also proactively reviewing that reporting to establish whether there is any evidence of offences".
When those allegations were first reported, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".
In a statement released on Friday, the Met said it had "received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s".
"Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers," the statement added.
Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney said: "We would encourage anyone who has been the victim of a sexual offence to come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.
"We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process."
Allegations against the entertainer and children's author were published after he lost a legal bid to stop claims against him being made public by the media.
Some of the women in the investigation accused Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.
One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault". Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.
He said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.
The Guardian and ITV News said that several of the women, who do not know one another, allege they were targets of unwanted sexual advances from Walliams.
The investigation also claimed Walliams had a sexual relationship with at least one junior employee at publisher HarperCollins, and pursued another.
Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.
In a letter addressed to journalists working on the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.
"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.
"And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."
He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."
Walliams shot to fame in the early 2000s with BBC sketch comedy Little Britain, served as a judge on ITV's Britain's Got Talent and launched a best-selling series of children's books.

The site of a car explosion that wounded Sergei Zavorotny in Moscow
A car bomb attack in Moscow has wounded a former adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov, Russia's Investigative Committee says.
Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was behind the wheel of his black Toyota when the explosion happened and Azarov told Russian TV his condition in hospital was "rather critical".
The car bomb went off a day after a Russian colonel was killed in another explosion in St Petersburg, and both blasts are seen as part of a series of attacks on military and prominent figures linked to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Zavorotny, 72, worked as a press aide to Mykola Azarov in Kyiv until 2014.
But when pro-Kremlin Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych was toppled from power, Azarov fled Kyiv for Russia and tried unsuccessfully to set up a government in exile.
In a 2020 US Senate report on interference in the 2016 American presidential election, Zavorotny is described at the time as an SVR [Russian foreign intelligence] officer involved in influence operations.
Russia's Investigative Committee said on Telegram on Friday: "Serhiy Zavorotny, a former adviser to the former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, was injured while driving a car. He was taken to one of the city hospitals, where he is receiving medical care."
It added: "A set of necessary investigative actions is being carried out. A number of examinations will be appointed, including medical and explosives."
According to several unconfirmed reports, Zavorotny suffered a number of serious injuries after an explosive device was detonated remotely.
Russia said the car bombs are the latest in a series of attacks targeting pro-Kremlin figures.
On Thursday a car bomb in the Pushkinsky District of St Petersburg killed a member of the Russian military, again after it was attached to the base of the car and detonated remotely.
The man targeted in the attack is yet to be named officially, but reputable sources suggest he was a high-ranking figure in the 6th Guards Air and Air Defence Forces Army.
Overnight into Friday, Ukraine and Russia exchanged attacks on each other's territories.
Ukrainian authorities said a hospital had been targeted by Russian bombardment.
They added that three people, including a 17-year-old boy, were also killed in attacks across southern Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.
Russia said a Ukrainian strike on an industrial facility in the central Samara region killed four people.
And in the southern Volgograd region another four died after an industrial zone was hit by drones. A further person died in the Bryansk border region, an area that is often fired upon.
Ukraine said these were retaliatory attacks in response to Russia's persistent targeting of its cities.

Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, the two leaders said in a joint statement. The defence pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.
Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday aimed at strengthening collective ​defence and promoting regional security, and pledged a unified stance against any external armed attack targeting either country, according to a joint statement issued after talks between their leaders.
The two ​sides ‌agreed to consult on threats to their security, as well ⁠as regional and global security issues and defence policies, and to expand cooperation through joint military exercises, defence-industry cooperation ‌and personnel training exchanges.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the accord during a meeting ⁠in Istanbul with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani. Qatar's ruler travelled to Istanbul after attending the United Nations COP31 climate summit in southern Turkey.

The agreement reflected the two countries' commitment to safeguarding their sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well ​as their shared vision of a more secure and stable ‌regional order, Turkey and Qatar said in the joint communiqué following the 12th session of their Supreme Strategic Committee.
"President Erdogan stated that we would continue working together to prevent the ‌resurgence of war in the Gulf region and establish a basis for dialogue and achieve peace," the Turkish presidency ​said in a statement on X.
The countries also expressed readiness to pursue energy cooperation, particularly in liquefied natural gas trade, building on their long-standing relationship, the joint statement ​added.

The Turkish presidency said Turkey and Qatar were working to develop and ​diversify their energy partnership and that their cooperation in the ​defence industry would continue to grow.
In August, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca , bringing ​together the Sunni Muslim US allies at a time of conflict across the region.
Ratified by the Turkish parliament last week, the so-called Mecca Joint Defence Agreement links NATO member Turkey, which has the alliance's second-largest military, with Pakistan, the Muslim world's only nuclear-armed state, and Saudi Arabia, the Gulf's leading power.
Read more Mecca pact nations hold talks with Iran to prevent renewed Middle East war
The pact clears the way for Ankara to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which has been struggling to fend off ⁠attacks by Yemen 's Iran-backed Houthi militants.
Turkey has said the agreement is not aimed at any other country and remains open to other states, including Egypt .
Under the agreement, signed by the three regional powers in August, ⁠an attack on ​one party constitutes an attack on all.

Moscow blames Kyiv for a series of car bombings that have targeted people linked to the war with Ukraine.
A car bombing in Moscow has critically injured an adviser to Ukraine’s former prime minister a day after a similar attack killed a military officer in St Petersburg.
The explosion on Friday was the latest in a series of bombings and shootings that have targeted people involved in the fighting in Ukraine. Moscow has blamed Kyiv for the attacks.
The Moscow explosion struck a car driven by Sergei Zavorotnyi, who previously worked as an adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, according to Russia’s Investigative Committee.
Zavorotnyi was hospitalised with injuries, the committee added. It did not identify possible suspects pending a criminal inquiry.
Azarov served as prime minister under Ukraine’s Moscow-friendly President Viktor Yanukovych, who was forced from office by protesters and fled to Russia in February 2014.
Azarov, who also lives in Russia, told state-run TV that he was “shocked” by the attack that left his former adviser critically injured. He said he believes Zavorotnyi was targeted because of his criticism of the Ukrainian government.
Zavorotnyi. 72, had worked as a journalist for Russia’s daily Komsomolskaya Pravda before becoming Azarov’s adviser. He wrote a book about Yanukovych’s ouster and ran an online outlet critical of Ukrainian authorities.
Russia’s REN TV channel said he lost his left arm, suffered multiple other injuries and was in a coma after the explosion.
Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow, said an explosive device was reportedly planted under the man’s car and detonated remotely as he was driving on Friday.
“The investigative committee has already launched a criminal case into this explosion,” she said.
A day earlier, in St Petersburg, a military serviceman was killed by a bomb in his vehicle, according to Russia’s Investigative Committee. It did not identify the victim or say who could be behind the bombing.
The Fontanka news outlet said Thursday’s victim was a colonel, while other Russian online media said the victim was a senior air force officer.
Shapovalova said preliminary reports indicated that the victim was a military serviceman, rather than a colonel of the Russian Air Force.
Like the attack on Friday, he was also driving the car when the bomb went off, she added.
“In both cases an explosive device was triggered remotely, and it was planted under their car,” Shapovalova said. “Here in Russia, all the attacks are considered to be orchestrated by the Ukrainian side.”

Parents take action while several independent bookshops say they had already stopped stocking his titles
In Sarah’s house, David Walliams has been a bedtime staple for years. Her children, aged eight, six and four, have dressed up as his characters for World Book Day – they love the over-the-top, unusual names and illustrations.
Now, all the books are going. “I’ll probably take them away and replace them with other authors,” says Sarah, a mother in west London. “Sooner rather than later, so they don’t realise.” If any of her children ask why, she will tell them “that his choices aren’t great and that I think we should be reading other books”.
This week a joint Guardian and ITV News investigation alleged that the children’s author used his position to pursue young women and girls for sex, including girls as young as 15. Walliams denies the allegations. HarperCollins stopped publishing new Walliams books last December and dropped his entire backlist in September.
For many independent children’s booksellers, the news only confirmed a decision made long ago.
Helen Tamblyn-Saville, owner of Wonderland Bookshop in Retford, Nottinghamshire, stopped stocking him in 2020. “They didn’t fit the ethos and values of my shop,” she says. Walliams’s books “punched down”, she believes, citing what she sees as “themes of racism, misogyny and classism” in his writings.
In 2021, HarperCollins removed a story about a Chinese boy – Brian Wong, Who Was Never, Ever Wrong – from future editions of The World’s Worst Children after complaints that it relied on harmful racial stereotypes.
In 2025, Tamblyn-Saville turned down an invitation to an event with him. “It feels very much as if the golden goose had to be protected, despite the clear red flags.”
Griffin Books in Penarth, south Wales, dropped his books about 18 months ago over “the low quality of the writing and his frequent use of offensive stereotypes”.
The Chicken and Frog bookshop in Brentwood, Essex, has not stocked him for a decade. Urmi, owner of Pickled Pepper Books in north London, has a blunter opinion: “We heard [rumours] about David Walliams at least five years ago and at that point chose to not stock his books,” she says. She believes that “everyone in the industry knew … so anyone that’s only just taking books off the shelf is only interested in profit”.
Mainstream stores have moved quickly. The Works, a budget retailer, said it had removed all David Walliams titles from sale and TG Jones confirmed it no longer sold his books in store or online. Waterstones said it was talking to HarperCollins about returning “the small number of copies which remain in stock in a few of our shops”.
Families are clearing their shelves too. One parent walked past a neighbourhood book-swap box this week and found it stuffed full of Walliams titles. Another mother joked that she would be burning hers, saying Walliams was “a knock-off Roald Dahl anyway”. Sarah hasn’t decided what to do with hers: giving them to a charity shop just puts them “back into the system”.
Walliams’ sales have been falling sharply – but they have not disappeared. Retailers sold 7,497 Walliams books over the past four weeks, worth £48,400, according to NielsenIQ BookData figures reported by The Bookseller.
In the same period last year, when he had a new book out, Walliams sold 102,000. Even so, almost 108,000 copies of his books have been sold so far this year, worth more than £702,000, and his titles have made more than £153m since 2008.
Public libraries are also facing a difficult decision. “This is a very sensitive issue involving deeply disturbing allegations, and some people may find the continued presence of these books upsetting,” said Isobel Hunter, CEO of the charity Libraries Connected.
“But we also have a long-established legal principle within the sector that all books should be available to the public unless the content itself is unlawful.
“So most library services have said that the books will remain in their collections until they are naturally weeded out and withdrawn under existing stock policy. That doesn’t mean, of course, that libraries are obliged to promote them or have them on display.”
Anecdotally, she said, demand had “dropped significantly in recent years”.
Some schools appear to be taking a harder line – several teachers told the Guardian they were removing Walliams books from their classroom shelves.
For Sarah, the principle is simple: “Kids need to understand that actions have consequences. If something’s not right, then we need to act upon it.”

Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy
A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips.
For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets.
With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years.
Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns.
But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere.
Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips.
It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations.
It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places.
They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties.
In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore.
The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere.
Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed.
But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department.
Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud.
In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months.
Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case.
Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing.
In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times.
Last year, Megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia could account for, according to a Bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses.
Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity.
On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government".
China has also long refuted accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips.
Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday following a board meeting
How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness.
In recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for Chinese companies, with tech firms such as TikTok and Manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largely views China positively.
For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law.
But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities.
Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case.
BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road.
In March 2023, a 7Road subsidiary in Singapore named Huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed.
Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man.
During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS.
Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences.
Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government.
Alice Huang, seen here in Taipei with Jensen Huang last year, ran Megaspeed for several months in 2023
"For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said.
Singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore".
But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips.
With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts.
Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.
Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said.
"Singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said.

No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure at Suffolk site affected, says US military
The US Air Force has said it responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday night at an RAF airbase in the east of England .
No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, the air force said.
Sirens were heard at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, one of several airbases in the UK used by the US military .
The USAF added: “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors and all of our families.
“Protecting our shared community is a joint responsibility, and we encourage everyone to support this effort by reporting any unusual or suspicious activity to local authorities.”
A UK Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: “We are coordinating with all relevant parties regarding reports of unauthorised drone activity at RAF Lakenheath this evening.
“USAF security forces personnel responded to the reports and the situation is now resolved. We are working closely with them to establish the facts. We will provide updates in due course.”
The MP for West Suffolk , Nick Timothy, said the authorities at the base had told him “there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved”.
He added: “Given the raised threat level, I continue to encourage everyone to report anything suspicious or out of the ordinary to the authorities.”
RAF Lakenheath said in September it was on “Charlie alert”, the second-highest threat level that can be issued by the US department of defense.
It is home to the 48th fighter wing, also known as the Liberty wing, with almost 7,000 active-duty personnel making it the largest US fighter operation in Europe, according to the official base website.
Earlier this year, police investigated an alleged terror plot at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire and a trespass incident at RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire. Both bases are used by the US Air Force.
In the past two months the US has evacuated planes from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk and RAF Fairford in response to suspected attacks on the bases allegedly linked to Iran.
Donald Trump said in October that “some threats” led the US to pull its bombers from Fairford.
Police said petrol but no explosives were found during searches of vans near the base in Gloucestershire.
Two men were charged by the Crown Prosecution Service over their alleged involvement in the incident.
This week, at least 12 USAF aircraft departed the nearby RAF Mildenhall base including two Boeing Stratotanker KC-135 refuelling aircraft, with one headed towards Germany and another seen landing at Prestwick airport near Glasgow.
Downing Street insisted earlier this week that British airbases are safe and their security is a “top priority”.

Galatasaray , Metin Öztürk ve Abdullah Kavukcu'nun istifalarını resmi olarak açıkladı.
Galatasaray’da 2’nci Başkan Metin Öztürk, görevlerinden istifa ettiğini sanal medya hesabından 1 Kasım 2026'da duyurmuştu.
Öztürk yaptığı açıklamada, “27 Ekim tarihli Yönetim Kurulu toplantımızda gerçekleşen, fiili saldırıya ve ölmüş anneme hakarete dönüşen eylemi kabullenmeme ne Galatasaray terbiyem ne annemden babamdan aldığım terbiyem el vermez. Bugün itibarıyla Galatasaray Yönetim Kurulu ve bağlı şirketlerdeki Yönetim Kurulu üyeliklerimden istifa ediyorum. Saygılarımla” ifadelerini kullanmıştı.
Galatasaray Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Abdullah Kavukcu da 1 Kasım 2026'da görevinden istifa ettiğini açıklamış ve 27 Ekim’de yapılan yönetim kurulu toplantısının ardından Metin Öztürk ile aralarında yaşanan tartışmanın sanal medyada gerçeği yansıtmayan ifadelerle aktarıldığını söyleyerek, "Galatasaray’a duyduğum sevgi ve sorumluluğum gereği, kişisel meselelerin kulübümüzün huzuruna, itibarına ve hedeflerine en küçük bir gölge dahi düşürmemesi adına yönetim kurulu üyeliği görevimden istifa etme kararı almış bulunuyorum" açıklamasında bulunmuştu.

Galatasaray Spor Kulübü yönetiminde üst üste yaşanan ayrılıklar kulüp tarafından resmen duyuruldu. Kulüp İkinci Başkanı Metin Öztürk'ün ardından Abdullah Kavukcu'nun da görevinden istifa ettiği açıklandı. Sarı-kırmızılı kulüp, Öztürk'ün ayrılığını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na yaptığı bildirimle doğruladı. İstifaların arkasında 27 Ekim 'de yapılan yönetim kurulu toplantısındaki tartışma bulunuyor.
Galatasaray , Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na yaptığı resmi bildirimle yönetimdeki ayrılığı doğruladı. Bildirimde Metin Öztürk'ün Galatasaray Sportif Sınai ve Ticari Yatırımlar A.Ş. Yönetim Kurulu üyeliğinden istifa ettiği duyuruldu. Kulüp bildirimde şu ifadelere yer verdi:
'Şirketimizin Yönetim Kurulu üyesi, Sayın Metin Öztürk Galatasaray Sportif Sınai ve Ticari Yatırımlar A.Ş. Yönetim Kurulu üyeliğinden istifa etmiştir. Kamuoyuna saygıyla duyurulur.'
Kulüp İkinci Başkanı Öztürk'ün ardından Abdullah Kavukcu'nun da görevinden istifa ettiği resmen açıklanmış oldu.
Galatasaray yönetim kurulunun 27 Ekim 'de yaptığı toplantıda disipline sevk konusundaki görüş ayrılığı, Metin Öztürk ile Abdullah Kavukcu arasında sert bir tartışmaya dönüştü. Öztürk toplantıda kendisine fiziki saldırı yapıldığını ve hayatını kaybeden annesine hakaret edildiğini iddia etti. Kavukcu ise aralarında sözlü bir tartışma yaşandığını kabul etti ve olayın sosyal medyada abartılarak yansıtıldığını savundu. İki yönetici de 1 Kasım'da istifa kararını kamuoyuyla paylaştı.
Metin Öztürk istifa kararını 1 Kasım'da sosyal medya hesabından şu ifadelerle duyurmuştu:
'Bugün itibarıyla Galatasaray Yönetim Kurulu ve bağlı şirketlerdeki Yönetim Kurulu üyeliklerimden istifa ediyorum. Saygılarımla.'
Galatasaray Sportif A.Ş. Başkan Vekili Abdullah Kavukcu da aynı gün yönetim kurulu üyeliğinden ayrıldığını açıkladı. Kavukcu kararını kulübün huzurunu ve itibarını korumak amacıyla aldığını belirtti ve kişisel anlaşmazlıkların kulübün hedeflerinin önüne geçmesini istemediğini söyledi. Yönetimden ayrılmasına rağmen kulübün başarısı için katkı sunmayı sürdüreceğini de bildirdi.

First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.
“This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.”
US Central Command denied that the radar system had been destroyed and said US forces had intercepted two Iranian drones headed for Bahrain .
Donald Trump has said in a series of media interviews over the past 24 hours that he will attack Iran only if necessary, claiming that Gulf countries, such as Saudi Arabia, have urged him to hold back from planned large-scale military strikes.
Trump said he had asked the vice-president, JD Vance, to end his interest in negotiating a new deal with Iran and instead focus on corruption and fraud in Democrat-run cities and states.
Vance had been seen by the Iranians as the most trustworthy figure close to Trump, but they had rejected his request for a personal meeting with their negotiators to discuss the terms of a peace deal.
Vance has been at the forefront of Republicans saying the war was the cause of the widespread Republican losses in the midterms. Trump said he had been disappointed in the American public because higher diesel prices were a small price to pay for preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.
An opinion poll in the UK showed 65% of the British public would oppose the US resuming the war in Iran, and only 14% would back it. The poll was conducted by YouGov for the Council for Arab-British Understanding (Caabu).
It also found 54% oppose UK bases being used by the US to mount attacks on Iran, with 29% in favour. Support for additional UK sanctions against Iran was 45%, with 22% opposed.
The poll was conducted on Tuesday and Wednesday this week, before two Iranians were found guilty on Thursday of spying and planning attacks on journalists in the UK. The Iranian embassy has rejected the court judgment as an attempt to advance a political agenda.
Chris Doyle, the director of Caabu, said: “The British public are sceptical about any war on Iran and what it might achieve. What might make the Burnham government take note is the very high level of opposition to any further war amongst 2024 Labour voters, at 79%.”
Iran’s Assembly of Experts, a body of elected Islamic jurists responsible for choosing the supreme leader, has become the first governing institution in Iran to call for a review of the country’s defence doctrine, potentially leading to religious permission for Iran to try to acquire a nuclear weapon.
In a statement released on Thursday, the assembly called for a review of Iran’s membership of the nuclear non-proliferation treaty, describing the move as an “unavoidable necessity” and a “public and national demand”.
The intervention carries a religious as much as political significance because the 88-strong assembly comprises senior clerics, most of whom are supposed to be qualified to exercise independent Islamic legal reasoning.
Iran has had a longstanding prohibition on nuclear weapons, based on a fatwa issued by the late supreme leader Ali Khamenei, but the relevance of the fatwa in the wake of the US attacks on Iran has been questioned widely in political and security circles.
Whether Iran has the stockpiles of uranium or technology to build a nuclear weapon is contested.
The UN nuclear inspectorate has expressed alarm about a continued lack of information from Iran about its nuclear sites. It said: “Our concerns are growing over Iran’s refusal to allow access to design information or inspections of the Isfahan facility. We do not know the exact location of the Isfahan uranium enrichment facility or whether it contains nuclear materials. It is imperative that we carry out our verification activities in Iran without further delay.”

Kızılcık Şerbeti 'nin beşinci sezonuna Lider karakteriyle katılan Murat Aygen, diziden iki bölüm sonra ayrılacağını duyurmasının ardından kararının perde arkasını ilk kez bu kadar ayrıntılı anlattı. ÇAPA TV'de İzzet Çapa'nın sunduğu Paşa Paşa Muhabbetler'e konuk olan oyuncu, hikayenin gidişatı, senaryoda gördüğü kritik bir cümle ve Lider'in akıbeti hakkında dikkat çeken sözler söyledi. Sunucunun 'Ölmeden çıktınız' sözüne verdiği 'benim için Lider öldü' yanıtı ise konuşmanın akılda kalan cümlesi oldu.
Gerçek adı Murat Ağlatçı olan oyuncu, 1971 Diyarbakır doğumlu ve Medcezir'de Faruk, Mucize Doktor 'da Profesör Doktor Tanju Korman, Yasak Elma'da Doğan Yıldırım karakterleriyle seyircinin yakından tanıdığı isimlerden biri. Kızılcık Şerbeti 'nin beşinci sezonunda Hilal'in kardeşi ve Kıvılcım'ın komşusu Lider olarak kadroya katılan Aygen, karakterin hikayesine duyduğu itirazı 30 Ekim 'de Gece Muhabiri'ne verdiği röportajda dile getirmiş, 'Ben bu adamı kabul etmedim açıkçası' diyerek iki bölüm sonra diziye veda edeceğini söylemiş, ayrılığın senarist değişikliğiyle ilgisi olmadığını da eklemişti. Kararının arkasındaki düşünceleri daha açık anlattığı konuşma ise ÇAPA TV'nin YouTube kanalında yayınlanan Paşa Paşa Muhabbetler programında geldi.
İzzet Çapa'nın konuğu olduğu programda ayrılık nedenini anlatan Aygen, hem yapım tarafıyla hem de yazan isimlerle çalışırken çok seçici davrandığını, role ilk teklif geldiğinde karakterin yapısı konuşulurken de toplantıda hikaye başka yere saparsa süreçten ayrılacağını söylediğini aktardı. Kötücül karakterler oynadığını hatırlatan oyuncu, Yasak Elma'daki Doğan'ın da eli çok temiz bir adam olmadığını ama kuralları olduğunu belirterek 'Ben cibilliyetsiz, pislik adam oynamayı sevmem' dedi; belirsizliklerin kendisinin takılabildiği yerler olmadığını ve oradan uzaklaşmak istediğini ekledi.
Senaryoda 'Liderin gerçek yüzü ortaya çıkar' cümlesini gördüğü anda menajerine yazdığını söyleyen Aygen'e göre bir ekip ayrılıp yeni bir ekip gelmiş, kurdukları hikaye de kendisine uymayınca süreç hızlıca noktalanmıştı. Sunucunun 'Ölmeden çıktınız' sözü üzerine 'benim için Lider öldü' diyen oyuncu, ayrılığı kibar bir dille ilettiğini, yapım tarafının da aynı şekilde karşılık verdiğini söyledi. Murat Aygen ayrılığını, 'Çok seçici davranıyorum. Bu hikaye başka yere saparsa ben kaçarım demiştim. Cibilliyetsiz, pislik adam oynamayı sevmem. Dizide ölmedi, ama benim için Lider öldü.' sözleriyle açıkladı.

Statement is rare instance of a prominent Jewish political leader taking a strong stand in defence of Arab Israelis
Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot accused caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fuelling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab minority, after he sought to delegitimise the community’s lawmakers by linking them to Hamas.
Eisenkot’s statement was a rare instance of a prominent Jewish political leader taking a strong stand in defence of Arab Israelis, who make up more than 20% of the population.
Two Arab-majority parties, Ra’am and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats in last month’s election, winning nearly a sixth of the 120-seat parliament and potentially emerging as kingmakers in efforts by Eisenkot to form a government.
“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” Eisenkot wrote on X on Friday.
“They have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation, fuelled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” he added.
“The attempt to marginalise them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of civic responsibility.”
Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly criticised leaders of Arab parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a “terror group” after its unprecedented 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.
All leaders of Arab parties have condemned the attack, in which Arab Israelis – descendants of Palestinians who remained in what became Israel in 1948 – were also among those killed.
Netanyahu has also repeatedly alleged electoral fraud by Arab-majority parties, but electoral authorities have rejected the claims.
In a speech, Netanyahu lamented that the two Arab lists refused to recognise Israel as a Jewish state, although Ra’am’s leader, Mansour Abbas, has done so in the past.
He further claimed that they sought to establish either an “Islamic state” or a “nationalist Palestinian state”.
During the same ceremony, the national security minister, Itamar Ben Gvir, heckled Joint List’s leader, Yousef Jabareen, during his oath of allegiance, accusing him of having “pledged allegiance to Hamas”.
“It is entirely legitimate to disagree with representatives of the Arab parties, even to strongly disapprove of some of them. But it is neither legitimate nor acceptable to malign an entire community, and I will not allow it,” Eisenkot said.
President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a new government on Sunday after consultations in which a majority of political parties, including the two Arab lists, recommended him for the role.
But one of Eisenkot’s rightwing allies, Avigdor Lieberman, has said he will back out of the coalition if Arab Israelis are part of it.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government within 28 days, he may request a 14-day extension. Should he still fall short, the mandate would pass to another lawmaker, most likely Netanyahu.

Kızılcık Şerbeti 'nde senaryo ekibinin değişmesinin ardından kadro hareketliliği sürüyor ve bu kez diziye ekrandan çok iyi tanıdığımız bir yüz dahil oluyor. Birsen Altuntaş'ın öğrendiğine göre Show TV 'nin uzun soluklu dizisine katılan isim, hikâyeye ticari bir hamleyle giriyor. Yeni karakterin kimin yanında yer alacağı ise şimdilik büyük merak konusu.
5 Ekim 1990'da İstanbul 'da doğan Birand Tunca, tiyatro eğitimini Müjdat Gezen Sanat Merkezi'nde aldı ve ekranla Diriliş: Ertuğrul'daki rolüyle tanıştı. İzleyicinin hafızasında en çok yer eden işi ise Erkenci Kuş'ta canlandırdığı Emre Divit karakteri oldu; Aşk Laftan Anlamaz gibi geniş kitlelerce izlenen yapımlarda da yer alan oyuncu, şimdi kadrosu kalabalık ve hikâyesi sürekli yön değiştiren bir dizinin içinde karşımıza çıkacak. Altuntaş'ın aktardığına göre Tunca, 148. bölümden itibaren Kızılcık Şerbeti 'nde Ali Murat adlı karakteri canlandıracak ve bu karakter dizinin hikâyesine iş dünyası üzerinden bağlanacak.
Kızılcık Şerbeti 'nde Ali Murat kim sorusunun şimdilik elimizdeki yanıtı, Erkan Avcı'nın canlandırdığı Asil'in iflas eden kanalını satın alan yeni patron olması. Tunca'nın karakteri bu hamleyle diziye hem para hem güç dengesi getiren biri olarak girerken, Ali Murat'ın hangi karakterlerle iş birliği yapacağı, Asil ile ilişkisinin nasıl şekilleneceği ve kimin partneri olacağı henüz bilinmiyor. Bu soruların yanıtı 148. bölümle birlikte netleşecek, ancak Tunca'nın katılımı dizideki değişimin yalnızca oyuncu kadrosuyla sınırlı kalmadığını da gösteriyor.
Altuntaş'ın haberine göre dizinin senaryosunu artık Ozan Yurdakul, Meryem Gür, Burcu Över ve Caner Güler yazıyor; ilk bölümden beri hikâyenin başında olan Melis Civelek ile Zeynep Gür ise görevi yeni ekibe devretmişti. Show TV 'nin cuma akşamlarına damga vuran dizisinde son haftalarda Nursema karakterinin geri dönüşü de gündem olmuştu ve Ali Murat'ın katılımı bu hareketliliğin yeni halkası olarak görülüyor. Gold Film yapımı dizi için yapım şirketi ya da kanaldan yeni oyuncuyla ilgili resmi bir açıklama gelmedi; bilgiler Altuntaş'ın kulis haberine dayanıyor.

Kızılcık Şerbeti ’nde sezon başında hikayesi yarım kalan Sevtap, yedi bölüm aradan sonra geri dönüyor. Ayrılık kararını menajerinden öğrendiğini ve bu duruma kırıldığını söyleyen Neslihan Yeldan, dönüşünü “Yarım kalmış bir dansımız, kapanmamış hesabımız vardı” sözleriyle duyurdu. Sevtap’ı yeniden Ünallar’ın hayatına sokan kişi ise torunu küçük Abdullah oldu.
Kızılcık Şerbeti ’nde Feyza Civelek’in canlandırdığı Nilay’ın annesi Sevtap’a hayat veren Neslihan Yeldan, beşinci sezon başlamadan kadrodan ayrılmıştı. Nilay’ın diziden ayrılmasının ardından Sevtap’ın hikayesinin de devam etmeyeceği basına yansıdı. Böylece Nilay üzerinden Ünallar’ın hayatına giren Sevtap, kendisine bir veda sahnesi yazılmadan diziden çıktı.
Yeldan, daha sonra yaptığı açıklamada ayrılık kararının yapımdan geldiğini anlattı. Oyuncunun aktardığına göre yeni sezon için ücret konusunda anlaşmışlardı. Buna rağmen yapım şirketi menajerini arayarak Sevtap’ın hikayesinin devam etmeyeceğini bildirdi. Yeldan, karakterin dizide bir süre daha kalabileceğini düşündüğünü ve hikayesinin bir final yazılmadan kesilmesine kırıldığını söyledi. O dönem tepkisini “Kırıldım ve sinirlendim” sözleriyle dile getirmişti.
Senaryo ekibindeki değişikliğin ardından Kızılcık Şerbeti ’nde sezon başında ayrılan karakterler yeniden gündeme geldi. Ceren Karakoç’un canlandırdığı Nursema’nın dönüşünün ardından sıra Sevtap’a geldi. Yeldan, Instagram ’da üzerinde “Sevtap is back” yazan bir set videosu paylaştı. Karakterle yarım kalmış bir dansları ve kapanmamış bir hesapları olduğunu söyleyen oyuncu, Sevtap’ın neşesi, tutkuları ve leopar deseniyle döneceğinin de haberini verdi.
Yeldan, Kızılcık Şerbeti ’ne dönüş heyecanını yeni projesi Who Are You? ’nun okuma provasında da paylaştı. Oyuncunun kadrosuna katıldığı gençlik dizisi, açılması planlanan 97 adlı dijital platform için hazırlanıyor.
Show TV ’nin paylaştığı bölüm bilgisine göre Sevtap, 13 Kasım tarihli bölümde torunu Abdullah’a duyduğu özleme dayanamayıp onu ziyarete geliyor. Nilay’ın annesi olarak tanıdığımız Sevtap, bu kez anneanne kimliğiyle hikayeye yeniden dahil oluyor. Küçük Abdullah’ı görmek için attığı bu adım, Sevtap’ın yolunu bir kez daha Ünallar’la kesiştiriyor.
Kanalın duyurusunda, bu ziyaretin ardından Ünallar’ın hayatında yeni gelişmeler yaşanacağı da belirtiliyor. Sevtap’ın dönüşüyle birlikte asıl merak edilen, torununu görmek için başlayan ziyaretin onu aileye ne kadar yaklaştıracağı. Kızılcık Şerbeti ’nin yeni bölümü 13 Kasım Cuma (bugün) saat 20.00’de Show TV’de ekrana geliyor.

MasterChef Türkiye'nin 12 Kasım akşamı yayınlanan yeni bölümünde haftanın üçüncü dokunulmazlık oyunu oynandı. Tolgahan ve Tolğa'nın kaptanlığında yarışan mavi ve kırmızı takım bir kez daha karşı karşıya geldi.
MasterChef'te haftanın 3'üncü dokunulmazlık oyununda konsept mantarlar oldu. Takımlar, farklı mantarlar ile hazırlanan yedi çeşit yemek için ter döktü.
Yarışmacılar 45 dakika içinde kendilerinden istenen mantarlı miso çorbası, Muğla usulü ekşili çintar, üç mantarlı kiş, mantarlı baklava böreği, kuzugöbeği mantar dolması, mantarlı risotto, mantarlı güveç için mücadele etti.
Hazırlanan yemeklerin tadımı sırasında stüdyoda gerginlik yaşandı. Tansiyonu düşen Tolğa toparlayıp yerine dönünce, kırmızı takımdaki Muhammed “Tolğa abi iyi misin?” diye sordu.
Tolğa da karşılık olarak “Tansiyonum düştü, ankastrem yok” deyince Muhammed, “Abi yapma şunu, ayıp. Kaç kere söyledim sana" diyerek sinirlendi.
Muhammed "Yapma abi şunu, ayıp" diye Tolğa'ya bağırınca şefler de sakinleşmeleri için müdaha etti. Tolğa şaka yaptığını söylese de sakinleşemeyen Muhammed izin isteyip stüdyodan çıktı.
Sonrasında şefler de neler olduğunu sordu. Konuşmalar sonucunda Muhammed'in anksiyete bozukluğu yaşadığı ve bu konunun gündeme getirilmemesini istediği ortaya çıktı. Tolğa ise onun kinayeli bir şekilde soru sorduğunu bu yüzden böyle bir cevap verdiğini öne sürdü.
Söz alan Armağan ise “Muhammed empati gücü yüksek bir adam, evde de bir diyaloglarını görmedim. Tolğa abinin mizacı sert biraz. Yanlış anladığını düşünüyorum. Bir insanın bir rahatsızlığı var. Bundan da muzdarip, ‘İyi misin Tolğa abi?’ sorusuna biraz sert bir cevap oldu bence” dedi.
Somer Sivrioğlu da anksiyete konusunun şaka yapılacak bir şey olmadığını söyledi.
Tüm bunların ardından dokunulmazlık oyununu kazanan taraf mavi takım oldu.
Takım oyununu kaybeden kırmızı takım, bireysel dokunulmazlık için tezgah başına geçti. Oyun öncesi konuşan Muhammed, “Geçmişte zor zamanlar geçirdim, ailem de hep yanımdaydı. Kimseye bel altı vurmayı tercih etmiyorum. Kimseyle bir uğraşım yok, eğer savaşacaksak bu yaralarımızdan olmasın. Eğer bunlar yapılmaya devam ederse ben de tepki göstermeye devam ederim. Bu tarz söylemler sonrası benim toparlamam 3-4 gün sürüyor. Ama şimdi yemeğimi yapıp rahatlayacağım” dedi.
Muhammed’den özür dileyen Tolğa da “İyi misin?’ diye sorunca ters anlamış olabilirim. Aramız kötü olunca niyet okumaya giriyor bazı şeyler. Bu 3 kere oldu, özür diliyorum. Hakkını helal et” dedi.
Hakkını helal ettiğini söyleyen Muhammed ise “Ben bunu atlatırken çok zor zamanlar geçirdim ve bunu atlattım. Ama bu söylemler beni zor duruma sokuyor. Benim Tolğa abiyle bir problemim yok, saygısızlık yapmadım, tartışmadım. Bir insanı yaralarından vurmak yakışmıyor. Ben yapmam, bana da yapılmasın” diye konuştu.
Şefler, bireysel dokunulmazlıkta kırmızı takım yarışmacılarından “Milyon Dolarlık Tavuk Kaserol” (Million Dollar Chicken Casserole) istedi.
Verilen sürede tabaklarını çıkaran kırmızı takım yarışmacılardan bireysel dokunulmazlığı kazan isim Tolgahan oldu. Gece sonunda arkadaşlarının oylarıyla eleme potasına giden de Bahar oldu.

UEFA turnuvalarının yayın hakları 2027-2028 sezonundan itibaren yeni bir adrese geçiyor. Hull City'nin sahibi Türk iş insanı Acun Ilıcalı , kararı sosyal medya hesabından duyurdu. Mevcut yayıncının UEFA ile yaptığı anlaşma bu sezon sonunda sona eriyor.
Hull City'nin sahibi Türk iş insanı Acun Ilıcalı , EXXEN platformunun önümüzdeki 4 yıl boyunca UEFA turnuvalarının yayın haklarını satın aldığını sosyal medya hesabından açıkladı. Ilıcalı paylaşımında şu ifadeleri kullandı:
'Avrupa futbolunun en prestijli organizasyonları, 2027-2028 sezonundan itibaren 4 yıl boyunca yeniden Exxen'de. UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi , UEFA Avrupa Ligi, UEFA Avrupa Konferans Ligi ve UEFA Süper Kupası'nın heyecanı, önümüzdeki 4 yıl boyunca Exxen ekranlarında olacak.'
Anlaşma Şampiyonlar Ligi , Avrupa Ligi ve Konferans Ligi'nin yanı sıra Süper Kupa'yı da kapsıyor. Yayınlar 2027-2028 sezonunda başlayacak ve 4 yıl boyunca sürecek. Yani üç kulüp turnuvası ile Süper Kupa aynı platformda toplanıyor.
Şampiyonlar Ligi , Avrupa Ligi, Konferans Ligi ve Süper Kupa 2024 yılından bu yana TRT ve Tabii platformundan izleniyor. TRT'nin UEFA ile yaptığı 3 yıllık anlaşma bu sezon sonunda tamamlanacak ve yayıncılık görevi 2027-2028 sezonunda Exxen 'e geçecek.

Dizilerin yayında kalıp kalmayacağını belirleyen reyting ölçümleri bu kez Rekabet Kurumu'nun mercek altında. Kurumun duyurduğuna göre televizyon izleyici ölçümlerine yönelik soruşturma başlatıldı; basına yansıyan bilgilere göre soruşturmanın muhatabı, reklamcılık sektörüne yönelik incelemede ulaşılan bulgular doğrultusunda resen harekete geçilen FIFTY5BLUE oldu. Milyarlarca liralık reklam bütçesinin hangi kanala gideceğini etkileyen sistemin nasıl işlediği artık resmen inceleniyor.
Soruşturmanın odağındaki FIFTY5BLUE, Kantar Media'nın Şubat 2026'da benimsediği yeni marka adı. Şirket, yatırım şirketi H.I.G. Capital'in satın almasının ardından bu isme geçerken izleyici ölçüm hizmetlerinde herhangi bir değişiklik olmadığını, müşteri temsilcilerinin de aynı kalacağını duyurmuştu. Televizyon izleyici ölçümü hizmeti verdiği için reyting tablolarının arkasındaki çalışma da bu şirketin elinden geçiyor. Rekabet Kurumu'nun incelemesi de tam olarak bu ölçüm sisteminin nasıl kurulup yönetildiğine odaklanıyor.
Haberlere yansıyan bilgilere göre soruşturma kapsamında ölçüme esas verilerin nasıl kullanıldığı, izleyici panelini oluşturan hanelerin nasıl seçilip yönetildiği, izleme kayıtlarının nasıl işlendiği ve sonuçların hangi yöntemle raporlandığı incelenecek. Kurum, bu uygulamaların televizyon reklamcılığındaki rekabet koşullarını nasıl etkilediğini değerlendirecek ve süreçlerin herhangi bir aşamasında rekabet kurallarının ihlal edilip edilmediğine bakacak. Soruşturmanın ne kadar süreceği ya da hangi sonuca varacağı henüz bilinmiyor. Konunun ağırlığı ise reyting rakamlarının sektörde neyi belirlediğine bakınca daha net anlaşılıyor.
Rekabet Kurumu'nun paylaşımında da vurgulandığı gibi reyting ölçümleri, televizyonda hangi programın yayında kalacağından milyarlarca liralık reklam bütçesinin hangi kanala gideceğine kadar dengeyi belirleyen bir ölçüt. Reyting verileri bir programı ya da kanalı kaç kişinin izlediğini, hangi izleyici gruplarına ulaştığını gösteriyor; reklamverenler ve medya ajansları da hedef kitleye ulaşmanın maliyetini bu rakamlara göre hesaplıyor. Kanallar ise izleyici gücünü bu sonuçlarla ortaya koyuyor ve reklam fiyatlarını da buna göre belirliyor. Kurum da güvenilir ve karşılaştırılabilir ölçüm sonuçlarının sektörün tamamı için önem taşıdığını vurguluyor.

Several hours later, the US military's Central Command, denied the IRGC's claim that the radar was destroyed and said it stopped two "one-way attack drones" targeting Bahrain by the militant group.
